title: Array templates and coordinated operations
summary: Pinned core array construction, add/remove, falsy insertion and source-inspected default scenarios; no executed Angular claims.

facts.claim: fieldArray is the item configuration template or function, while fieldGroup holds the current child fields. FieldArrayType sizes fieldGroup to the array model, clones new item configurations and assigns string index keys unless the cloned item key is null.
conditions: FieldArrayType.onPopulate is running; a non-array model gives a target child count of zero.
For a keyed array field, the implementation registers an existing control if found, otherwise a new FormArray.
A function-valued fieldArray is called with the array field itself before its returned configuration is cloned.
limits: A key of null is deliberately retained on a cloned item; do not assert that every child always receives an index key.
This describes source behavior at 6.3.12, not execution of a consuming Angular application.
facts.context: Repeatable arrays: fieldArray template versus instantiated fieldGroup children, function templates, FormArray registration and conditional index keys.
facts.source_quote: `fieldGroup` is the current child-field collection; `fieldArray` is the template or function used to create item fields. A `FieldArrayType` implementation registers a FormArray, sizes its fieldGroup to the model array, clones each item config, and assigns index keys when applicable [K12](sources.md#k12).

facts.claim: FieldArrayType.add(index?, initialModel?, options?) inserts a model item, rebuilds the associated fields and emits a fieldChanges valueChanges event; with an omitted or null index it appends at the current fieldGroup length. With omitted options it marks the array control dirty.
conditions: Use an initialized FieldArrayType with its expected array model and control; when its model is absent the method initializes an empty array.
The markAsDirty option controls the explicit dirty marking; { markAsDirty: false } suppresses that marking.
Passing an empty options object {} also supplies no truthy markAsDirty flag, so it skips the explicit dirty marking; the true default applies when the options argument is omitted or undefined.
At the requested insertion index, the method inserts a clone of a truthy initialModel; falsy initialModel takes the undefined branch before the rebuild.
limits: Suppressing dirty marking does not suppress the rebuild or valueChanges event, and does not reset an already dirty control to pristine.
Manually splicing fieldGroup alone does not perform this model mutation, rebuild and event sequence.
Insertion uses JavaScript splice semantics; this fact does not promise validation of arbitrary out-of-range indices.
facts.context: Repeater add operation, append or insertion index, initial model, markAsDirty option and coordinated rebuild/change notification.
facts.source_quote: Use the array type's `add(index?, initialModel?, options?)` and `remove(index, options?)` when implementing its UI. These operations update model/field collections, rebuild, emit changes, and normally mark the control dirty. Manually splicing only fieldGroup bypasses some of that coordination [K12](sources.md#k12).

facts.claim: FieldArrayType.remove(index, options?) removes the indexed model item and child field, updates remaining item keys, unregisters the removed control, rebuilds associated fields and emits a fieldChanges valueChanges event. With omitted options it marks the array control dirty.
conditions: Use an existing array item index in an initialized FieldArrayType.
Key updates apply to keyed fields; for a keyless grouping the implementation descends into its child fields.
Passing { markAsDirty: false } suppresses the method's explicit dirty marking.
Passing an empty options object {} also supplies no truthy markAsDirty flag, so it skips the explicit dirty marking; the true default applies when the options argument is omitted or undefined.
limits: Removing only a fieldGroup entry omits the coordinated model, control, rebuild and notification operations.
No guarantee for invalid removal indices or arbitrary custom grouping is established.
Suppressing dirty marking does not make an already dirty control pristine or suppress the change event.
facts.context: Repeater remove operation, model splice, child unregister, remaining index keys, rebuild, valueChanges and markAsDirty.
facts.source_quote: Use the array type's `add(index?, initialModel?, options?)` and `remove(index, options?)` when implementing its UI. These operations update model/field collections, rebuild, emit changes, and normally mark the control dirty. Manually splicing only fieldGroup bypasses some of that coordination [K12](sources.md#k12).

facts.claim: In Formly 6.3.12, FieldArrayType.add uses the truthiness of initialModel: truthy values are cloned, while false, zero and an empty string take the undefined insertion branch.
conditions: The value is supplied as the second argument to FieldArrayType.add.
limits: The subsequent build and item defaults can affect the resulting model; the insertion branch is not a promise of the final value.
Do not assume this method preserves a falsy scalar unchanged or invent a universal workaround without checking the intended model shape.
This is scoped to the pinned implementation, not earlier or later releases.
facts.context: Falsy scalar values false, 0 and empty string passed as initialModel to array add; truthiness and default-value boundary.
facts.source_quote: Important exact-version detail: this implementation tests `initialModel` for truthiness before cloning it. Do not assume passing false, zero, or an empty string to `add` preserves that scalar unchanged; establish the intended model shape and verify that use case [K12](sources.md#k12).

facts.claim: The inspected 6.3.12 array tests expect defaultValue [null] to create one child with resetFieldOnHide enabled, expect a hidden defaulted array to have no model/children until shown, and expect add(0) in the specific item-default fixture to produce ['default', null].
conditions: These are assertions read in K27, not upstream tests executed in this batch.
The insertion fixture sets array defaultValue: [null], resetOnHide: true, fieldArray type: input with defaultValue: 'default' and expressions.hide returning false, plus extras.resetFieldOnHide: true.
The hide/show fixture explicitly invokes expression checking and change detection after setting hide to false.
The insertion test calls change detection after add(0) before asserting the model.
limits: Do not generalize these fixtures into universal default/reset/hide ordering or a tested Material repeater recipe.
Earlier patch compatibility has not been checked.
Existing reset-on-hide child cleanup support is reused through the related fact rather than duplicated.
facts.context: Source-inspected default array, hide/show and item-default insertion scenarios; add at index zero and exact fixture boundaries.
facts.source_quote: Default values and hide/show behavior interact with item creation. The inspected test section covers default array values, hiding/showing, and insertion at a specific index. These tests supply useful regression scenarios but were not run here [K27](sources.md#k27). Earlier patches need separate checking against [patch history](sources.md#k29).
